author: jojobloblo
body: Alright, here's what's up. So me, and many other Avicus players, have some pretty freaking severe OCD. Whenever I start a game, like everyone else, I'm going to want an inventory that helps with PvP and rushing. For me I also need it to satisfy my OCD. Well, when you spawn, you get the arrangement of what the map creator decides. That decision may not be suitable for you as a player. Ok I'm starting to somewhat rant. What I'm suggesting is an inventory organizer. What you'd be able to do is in the hub or spectator mode, you can select "Inventory Organizer" in your hotbar. When you click it, you can select a Nebula map. Once you click that map, the inventory screen pops up, including armor view and crafting table. You can move things around and if it suits your fancy, craft the wood into planks, or stone into stone bricks. In my opinion this would be a feature extraordinarily helpful and I would love to see it be added.

replies.author: _DC
replies.body:
This is a great idea.
The only problem would be that, as @vsplesk101 mentioned, you would have to have a kind of "profile" for every player on the server as everyones ideal inventory setup is different.

As a plugin is a server side modification, you can not add on-screen buttons or UI of any kind (Apart from the 1.8 text overlay that can be triggered from a plugin). This means that you would have to type a command into chat to order you inventory. It's probably quicker just to order you inventory yourself if you had to type a command.

replies.author: _DC
replies.body:
Your calculation was pure estimation. If memory was a problem you could compress it rather neatly with bitwise operations.

So each item will need a variable for the 'id' and 'place' in the inventory. With the 'place' you can use 9 bits as you would only need the hotbar items to be in the correct place. To compact the 'id' instead of using Minecraft's item id, we will just make this an index from 0 to the amount of items that are given to the player at the start of a match. This 'id' number is a correlation to the order in which the items are defined in the YML.
If this was for Senex II for example, you would need another 9 bits for the number of different items you get at the start minus the armour.

This all means that each player will need 18 bits to store it's hotbar information. As you say: "No, there will be like max. 5000 people which will use this."

5000 * 18 bits  = 90000 bits
90000 bits = 11.25 kilobytes

11.25 kilobytes space will be used to store 5000 players.
It would be a bit hard though to use two 9 bit segments when a byte is 8 bits. So you may just want to use 32bits(4 bytes) for each one  just to make it easier.
